page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, and 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, such as in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, falls into the lower 25% tier, with single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom 10%. However, the 24-vCPU configuration elevates multi-core performance to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth also performs consistently in the middle tier, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 983.75 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 90.83 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge utilizes mature Intel Xeon hardware, offering a stable and dedicated resource pool without the premium associated with newer-generation architectures. This makes it a viable option for workloads that benefit from multi-threaded execution but do not require cutting-edge single-core speeds. Recommended workloads include general-purpose applications, static web serving, multi-threaded compilation tasks, and database operations that fit within the 96.0 GB memory footprint.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.6xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Benchmark data shows that while single-core performance is relatively weak, multi-core execution and memory bandwidth reside firmly in the average tier. This hardware profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for multi-threaded workloads that do not demand the highest single-core speeds. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, database operations, and software compilation.
